Trail Technology · Unit 7: Electricity · Module 3

Electric Potential and Capacitors

Voltage as energy per charge, potential energy, equipotentials and capacitors.

Lesson coming

The question

What does the 36 V on an e-bike battery actually mean?

The physics

  • Electric potential and potential energy
  • Voltage
  • Electric field strength
  • Equipotential surfaces
  • Capacitors
  • Energy in capacitors

The math

  • V = ΔPE / q
  • E = QV (energy, battery approximation)
  • C = Q / V
  • U = ½CV²

Learning objectives

  • Explain voltage as energy per unit charge
  • Calculate the energy a battery stores, in joules and watt-hours
  • Calculate capacitance and the energy a capacitor stores
  • Interpret equipotential lines and field strength

Helps to know first: Electric Charge and Electric Field.

The mountain biking connection

A battery’s voltage tells you the energy each coulomb of charge carries. Its charge rating and voltage together set how much energy it stores.
